name: Industrial Engineering
boundaries: Industrial Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Universal first-principles theory of factory physics
original_dispositions.reason: Existing production theory already provides useful relationships, while an exact theory for every system with instant optimization is not a supported, sufficiently distinct candidate in this review. Relevant transferable production and disruption capabilities are considered in IND-01 and IND-03, but neither is a universal factory theory.

original_dispositions.original_title: Polynomial-time exact solver for all NP-hard industrial problems
original_dispositions.reason: The underlying general complexity breakthrough belongs centrally to mathematics and computer science; industrial scheduling and routing are major applications. The claimed universal practical solver also has no demonstrated basis here.

original_dispositions.original_title: Complete predictive model of human performance, error and fatigue
original_dispositions.reason: Added as IND-05, narrowed to transferable and prospectively validated prevention of work-related risk. The universal prediction and elimination claims are not retained.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfect enterprise-scale digital twin with autonomous control
original_dispositions.reason: A twin is a possible enabling technique rather than a clearly separate demonstrated end capability at the requested impact standard. Relevant uses overlap with IND-01 and IND-02. The historical numerical gains and zero-intervention claim are unsupported here.

Covered in part by IND-04. Economical recovery of mixed products is the retained underlying capability. The historical claim of universal, lossless material and energy closure is not established; recovery still needs energy and can involve material losses.
Covered by IND-03, narrowed to specified shocks, explicit assumptions and measured intervention costs. Continuity under any shock without buffers or cost is not claimed.

original_dispositions.original_title: Theory of knowledge-work productivity and innovation flow
original_dispositions.reason: The ambition is important, but the historical entry does not identify a sufficiently concrete, evidenced field-centered capability at revolutionary scale. Claimed five- to tenfold innovation gains are unsupported.

As stated, it assumes away uncertainty, capacity constraints and physical transit. More capable reconfiguration and disruption containment are addressed separately in IND-01 and IND-03; neither promises buffer-free global operation.

original_dispositions.original_title: Inherent safety and error-proofing for socio-technical systems
original_dispositions.reason: Added as IND-06, restricted to enforceable constraints for specified hazards and operating envelopes. A universal guarantee against all catastrophic error is not retained.

original_dispositions.original_title: Global multi-objective optimization of profit, planet and people
original_dispositions.reason: Multi-objective methods can make trade-offs explicit, but Pareto optimality does not eliminate them or determine whose preferences should prevail. The historical entry supplies no concrete new capability or evidence sufficient to establish a separate revolutionary addition.

reconciliation_change_log.reason: Their identities and proposed demonstrations remain intact. The supply-network entry now cites the accessible arXiv record for the Inoue–Todo working paper; the original SSRN page could not be opened.

The historical human-performance concept has a potentially transformative, field-centered core when narrowed to transferable, validated prevention of work-related risk. The evidence does not support prediction of every individual and team outcome in every setting.

The historical safety-design concept has a distinct, potentially transformative core when restricted to specified hazards and verifiable operating assumptions. It overlaps with IND-05 where human behavior affects safety, but its central advance is system architecture and assurance rather than performance prediction.

The historical list’s asserted institutional endorsement of all ten topics is unverified. The exact IISE, INFORMS and NSF links supplied could not be opened in this review; the supplied journal-volume link returned a forbidden response. The named IISE Transactions perspective was not independently verified. These access failures do not, by themselves, prove that the documents do not exist, but they do not support the historical answer’s claims.
